newsitem.title: USA: Warmer forecasts support U.S. spot natgas prices.
newsitem.headline: Warmer forecasts support U.S. spot natgas prices.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices on Friday were up slightly in the Midwest and Gulf markets ahead of warmer weather this weekend but softer in the West, industry sources said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices were quoted about one cent higher at $2.15-2.16 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub as temperature highs reached into the mid-90s F.
In the Permian Basin market, however, prices slid four cents to about $2.02, pressured by the usual drop in demand over a weekend.

Like the Permian market, southern California border prices fell by about five cents to about $2.20. Temperatures in southern California were forecast to hover around highs of about 80 degrees F this weekend, according to Weather Services Corp.

The extensive outage list in the West prevented prices from falling further, traders said. The 750 megawatt (MW) Navajo 1 coal unit in Arizona was set to shut tonight through Monday morning for repairs.
The 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal plant in New Mexico is also expected to shut Friday for three weeks for repairs.
Southern California Edison's 750 MW Mohave 2 coal unit in Nevada remained off line and no estimate on when the unit would restart was yet available.
Also, the 1,080 MW San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in California was expected to remain off line until the middle of next week.
The adjacent unit 3, with a generating capacity of 1,080 MW, was also slated to restart next week, according to the company.

In the Midwest, swing prices were steady to up about one cent to about $2.02-2.04. Chicago city-gate prices were quoted equally firmer around $2.19 in anticipation of highs around 90s degrees F this weekend and into early next week.
In the East, swing prices at the New York city-gate held in the high-$2.30s despite the arrival of warmer weather and nuclear outages.
Niagara Mohawk said its 610 MW Nine Mile Point 1, shut today for valve repairs, was expected to return to service early next week.
